intent.instructions: You are playing a rolling scrap mech in a roguelite stage. The mechanics: you damage enemies only by landing on them from above, or by ramming while above the fast speed tier, so speed is what makes combat possible. A difficulty tier rises on a fixed timer and raises enemy health, spawn rate and cache prices. Caches cost scrap and grant permanent stacking buffs that last the rest of the run. Scrap has no use other than buying caches, so scrap still held at the end of the run bought nothing. Choose the single best intent to hold for the next second or two.

danger.instructions: How much immediate danger is the player in right now, given health and the listed threats?
criteria: Safe: free to optimise purely for speed and loot
Pressured: threats must be accounted for in the next move
Critical: about to take a hit that matters, or low enough that another hit ends the run

greedy.instructions: Would taking more loot or another cache right now cost more, in rising difficulty and risk, than the value it adds to this run?

rationale.intent: One narrow judgement: given what is reachable right now, what next? Mechanics only. An earlier version of this instruction said that scrubbing speed "costs you" and that time spent is "never free", which is a valuation, not a rule. A negative control caught it: with that wording the model declined a cache priced at zero scrap, 0.18 against 0.81. The sweep built on it was measuring the prompt. State what the game does and let the judgement be the judgement.
rationale.danger: Asked in the same request, so it costs one round trip rather than two.
rationale.greedy: Separate from the intent so policy can veto greed without re-asking.
